facts.fact_text: Both applicants participated in a number of unauthorised peaceful demonstrations organised by the opposition.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
In the course of many of those unauthorised peaceful demonstrations, both applicants were arrested and convicted.
Both applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations of the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.
According to the applicants, they were never served with a copy of the administrative-offence reports or with other documents from their case files following their arrests during the demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrests during the demonstrations or while they were in police custody.
Prior to the demonstration of 20 October 2012, on 15 October 2012 the organisers gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
Prior to the demonstration of 17 November 2012, on 12 November 2012 the organisers gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the site indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed another location for the demonstration of 20 October 2012, namely the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District on the outskirts of Baku.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted in general terms that the assembly of 17 November 2012 would not be in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the assembly of 17 November 2012 itself would be impractical.

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, which entered into force on 1 July 2011, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that a copy of the administrative offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to the administrative offence proceedings or to a representative of a legal entity.

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, which entered into force on 1 July 2011, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an aggrieved person in administrative offence proceedings has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding free and fair elections.
The participants in the demonstrations were protesting against impediments on freedom of assembly.
According to the applicants, they were never served with a copy of the administrative-offence reports or with other documents from their case files following their arrests during the demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrests during the demonstrations or while they were in police custody.
According to the applicants, the respective hearings before the Sabail District Court were very brief.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Sabail District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.
